title: Docebo vs. Gloat: AI Workforce Readiness Platform Comparison
summary: Choosing between Docebo and Gloat comes down to the delivery of training content and how talent gets deployed globally across your organization.
body_markdown:
Choosing between Docebo and Gloat comes down to one question: who owns and executes the upskilling and reskilling your workforce needs, and who just points to where it happens?


Both are leading enterprise platforms for workforce agility, but they solve it from very different architectural angles.


- **Docebo** , now powered by 365Talents, is a dual learning and skills platform that closes the loop from skill gap to learning to verified readiness.
- **Gloat** is an AI-native Agentic HR platform that orchestrates skills, talent, workforce planning, HR operations, and learning and development on top of your existing HCM and learning systems.


This guide compares them on features, skills management, internal mobility, compliance, integrations, pricing, and real customer reviews so you can decide which platform fits your organization best.


## **Docebo vs. Gloat at a glance**


Here’s how the two platforms compare across the criteria enterprise buyers weigh most.

## **When is Docebo the right fit?**


Choose Docebo when learning and skill building sit at the center of your workforce strategy, or when you have a board mandate for enterprise-wide transformation that requires upskilling or reskilling.


- **You need to build missing skills, not just match existing ones.** Docebo, powered by 365Talents, identifies skill gaps and delivers targeted learning pathways in the same platform. You move from detecting a gap to closing it without stitching together separate tools, which is the essence of skills-based learning.
- **You require strict compliance and audit-ready certification.** Docebo supports observation checklists, and e-signatures, with audit trails and automated recertification. A talent marketplace can’t run compliance training or prove certification to a regulator, so this is table stakes only Docebo meets.
- **You need to train external audiences like customers and partners.** Docebo’s extended enterprise runs white-labeled sub-portals for customers, partners, and vendors, with multilingual support and ecommerce for selling courses. Gloat is built for internal employees only.
- **You want to consolidate your learning, skills, and mobility stack.** One contract combines the LMS, authoring tools, skills intelligence, and internal mobility. That lowers total cost of ownership and cuts the vendor sprawl that comes from buying a marketplace, an LMS, and a skills tool separately.
- **You need governed, multi-signal skills validation.** Skills are validated through real work, course completions, project outcomes, and manager input, not a single self-added profile tag. That gives leaders a defensible view of readiness for[upskilling and reskilling](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/employee-upskilling-reskilling/) , and it makes generative AI recommendations far more accurate.


## **When is Gloat the right fit?**


Gloat is the stronger pick when you want a broad Agentic HR and workforce orchestration layer that sits on top of the systems you already run.


- **Your primary focus is an agile, internal gig economy.** Gloat lets managers post short-term projects and gigs quickly, then matches employees by skills and interests. It’s purpose-built for putting spare capacity to work fast, and it routes any learning to the systems you already run rather than delivering it itself.
- **You need to break down silos and retain talent.** Gloat gives cross-departmental visibility in large, matrixed organizations, surfacing opportunities employees would never find on their own. That visibility can lift engagement and retention.
- **You want to scale peer-to-peer mentorship.** The platform matches mentors and mentees on goals and interests, making talent mobility feel personal even at enterprise scale.
- **You already have a deeply entrenched enterprise LMS.** Gloat is positioned as an orchestration layer that connects to your existing LXP and LMS rather than replacing them. If you’re happy with your learning platform and only need Gloat to identify gaps and route people to it, that’s a clean fit.
- **You need rapid time-to-value for lightweight opportunity matching.** Gloat delivers a dedicated project and opportunity board without re-architecting your learning stack, so a focused rollout can show results quickly.


## **Docebo vs. Gloat: detailed platform and capability breakdown**


The skills gap is now the top barrier to business transformation, cited by 63% of employers in the[World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2025](https://www.weforum.org/press/2025/01/future-of-jobs-report-2025-78-million-new-job-opportunities-by-2030-but-urgent-upskilling-needed-to-prepare-workforces/) , which also projects that 39% of workers’ core skills will change by 2030. That pressure is exactly what both platforms address, so the details of how they do it matter. Here’s how the two stack up across the nine capability areas buyers evaluate most.


### **Core system architecture and primary job to be done**


Docebo is an enterprise learning management system that manages, delivers, and tracks training across multiple audiences, now with a skills intelligence layer from 365Talents. Its job is to turn capability gaps into learning and measurable outcomes.


Gloat is an AI-native Agentic HR and workforce orchestration platform that spans skills intelligence, talent management, talent acquisition, workforce planning, HR operations, and learning and development.


As of March 2026, Gloat repositioned around[Agentic HR](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260331249744/en/Gloat-Introduces-Agentic-HR-The-End-of-Reactive-HR) , with AI agents that reason and act as an orchestration layer on top of existing HCM and learning systems like Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, and Oracle, without replacing them. Gloat can surface skill gaps, recommend opportunities and learning, and route people to the right systems, but the learning itself runs elsewhere.


Gloat sits on top of your existing learning platform; Docebo is the learning platform. That architectural split shapes almost every other difference on this list.


### **Skills intelligence and data governance**


[Docebo Skills Intelligence](https://www.docebo.com/products/skills-intelligence/) , powered by 365Talents, infers and continuously updates skills from real work, learning activity, job history, and manager validation, all inside a governed skills and job architecture.


Docebo[acquired 365Talents](https://www.docebo.com/365talents/) in[January 2026](https://www.docebo.com/company/newsroom/docebo-acquires-365talents/) , to bring skills and learning together.[Recognized by Forrester](https://365talents.com/en/resources/365talents-named-forrester-skills-intelligence-solutions/) in its Skills Intelligence Solutions Landscape 2026, 365Talents already serves more than[two million users in 60+ countries](https://brandonhall.com/docebos-acquisition-of-365talents-moving-from-skills-intelligence-to-skills-action/) , and is ISO 42001 certified for responsible AI.


Gloat also infers skills, but it treats them primarily as profile tags that power matching rather than a governed, multi-signal system of record.


As Docebo CEO Alessio Artuffo put it, most vendors help you collect and analyze skills, but[very few help you act on them](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260120961187/en/Docebo-Acquires-365Talents) . If you need consistent, comparable skills data across HR and learning, Docebo goes deeper.


### **Internal mobility and opportunity matching**


This is Gloat’s home turf. Its consumer-grade experience surfaces gigs, projects, and roles fast, and reviewers consistently praise how quickly matching happens.


Docebo also delivers[internal mobility](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/internal-mobility/) , but it ties mobility to skill readiness and structured career paths, so an employee who isn’t ready for a role sees the exact learning to get there.


For pure, high-velocity gig matching, Gloat is excellent. For talent mobility connected to development and verified readiness, Docebo’s closed loop wins.


### **Learning execution and content management**


Docebo runs a[native LMS](https://www.docebo.com/products/learn-lms/) with generative AI authoring, neural search, social learning, gamification with leaderboards, and the Go.Learn mobile app for offline access. It delivers[corporate training](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/employee-training/) , connects to Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom for virtual sessions, and pulls in content from LinkedIn Learning, Go1, and OpenSesame.


Gloat doesn’t own an LMS or deliver learning itself. It can surface skill gaps, recommend learning tracks, and route people to the learning systems you already run, including through its Learning and Reskilling agent, but the delivery, management, tracking, and validation happen in your existing LMS or LXP.


If you want to build, deliver, and validate learning in one place, only Docebo does it natively.


### **Extended enterprise and external training**


Docebo’s extended enterprise runs distinct, white-labeled sub-portals for customers, partners, and vendors from one platform, each with its own branding, content, ecommerce, and reporting. That makes it a fit for customer education and partner enablement, not just employee training.


Gloat is built for the internal workforce only and has no extended enterprise capability.


If external audiences are in scope, this is a decisive gap.


### **Compliance training and certification management**


Docebo has observation checklists for on-the-job (OTJ) training and e-signature features built-in, with automated certification, recertification schedules, and audit trails built for regulated industries.


Gloat offers no compliance training or certifications; it isn’t designed for that job.


For any organization with regulatory compliance obligations, Docebo is the only workable option of the two.


### **Implementation and onboarding**


Docebo provides vendor-led onboarding, administrator training, and taxonomy mapping to get your LMS and skills data in order.


Gloat implementations are change-management heavy: managers have to post gigs, and employees have to build profiles for the marketplace to work.


Both require effort, but the risk profiles differ. Docebo’s success depends on content and configuration, while Gloat’s depends on sustained manager and employee participation.


### **Customer support and vendor accountability**


Docebo offers ticketing, email, and phone support, customer success managers, and SLAs, backed by a base of more than 3,900 organizations.


Gloat provides enterprise support focused on marketplace adoption and maintaining HRIS integrations with systems like Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, and Oracle HCM.


Both serve large enterprises; the difference is scope, since Docebo supports the full learning lifecycle and Gloat supports the marketplace layer.


### **Pricing and total cost of ownership**


Both platforms are enterprise, quote-only, with no public pricing. For total cost of ownership, Docebo consolidates the LMS, skills intelligence, and internal mobility into a single contract, while Gloat is a premium marketplace priced separately on top of the LMS you already pay for.


Third-party benchmarks, which are not official Docebo pricing, estimate enterprise Docebo contracts averaging around $185,000 per year; treat any such figure as an industry estimate.


For most buyers, consolidation favors Docebo on total cost.


## **Docebo vs. Gloat: what customers say**


Ratings and enterprise results tell a consistent story.


On[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/docebo-inc) , Docebo holds 4.3 out of 5 across 750 reviews, and on Capterra it holds 4.4 out of 5 across[242 reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/127213/Docebo/reviews/) , with strong marks for ease of use and reporting. Gloat holds 4.4 out of 5 on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/gloat/reviews) , but across just 34 reviews; its Capterra listing is a single review from 2019, so it isn’t statistically representative.


Gloat reviewers praise the user experience and onboarding. One enterprise HR reviewer noted that people find onboarding easy and that “[matching happens so quickly](https://www.g2.com/products/gloat/reviews/gloat-review-10148008) !” Another highlighted a “[fantastic user interface and user experience](https://www.g2.com/products/gloat/reviews/gloat-review-7843398) ” that minimizes the effort to log skills and goals. For balance, a[verified financial services reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/gloat/reviews/gloat-review-10062393) praised the functionality and working relationship but flagged slow product enhancements.


Docebo reviewers focus on measurement and multi-audience delivery. One LMS admin said the “[reporting and tracking features](https://www.capterra.com/p/127213/Docebo/reviews/) are particularly helpful for monitoring progress and measuring learning outcomes.” A program manager valued delivering “a[diverse and organized digital library](https://www.capterra.com/p/127213/Docebo/reviews/) to various target groups (customers, partners, staff),” a nod to extended enterprise.


Enterprise results back the skills story. At[SNCF](https://365talents.com/en/resources/case_studies/customer-success-story-sncf-365talents/) , the French national railway with 153,000+ employees, 94% had active skills profiles within 6 months, and the organization has[saved €100 million](https://365talents.com/en/lp/2026-skills-impact-report/) on temping and external consulting; the program won a Digital HR Awards 2024.


At[Société Générale](https://365talents.com/en/resources/case_studies/client-use-case-societe-generale/) , with nearly 74,000 employees, staff consult[more than 25,000 internal opportunities](https://365talents.com/en/lp/experience-365talents/) every month. At SEGULA Technologies,[adoption reached 80% to 81%](https://365talents.com/en/lp/experience-365talents/) among employees in France. These are 365Talents deployments, the skills intelligence engine now inside Docebo, and they show talent development measured by real adoption, not adjectives.


## **5 Questions to ask during your platform demos**


Bring these requests to every demo and watch how each vendor responds:


1. Show how an employee who lacks a required skill for a gig is routed to the exact training needed to acquire it
2. Demonstrate compliance recertification and SCORM or xAPI content upload
3. Show how you validate a skill through real work, not a self-added profile tag
4. Launch a branded extended enterprise portal for customers or partners
5. Show reporting that ties learning activity to internal mobility and business outcomes


## **Which platform is the right choice for your team?**


Start with the job you need done. Rather than asking which platform is objectively better, ask whether you need to build capabilities through learning or match existing skills to short-term work.


- **Do you need to close skill gaps through training, or match existing skills to short-term projects?** If you need to build capability, choose Docebo; if you only need to match, choose Gloat.
- **Are you training external audiences or managing regulatory compliance?** If yes, Docebo is the only option of the two.
- **What’s your enterprise HR tech stack strategy, consolidate or overlay?** To consolidate learning, skills, and mobility in one contract, choose Docebo; to add a mobility layer on top of an entrenched LMS, Gloat fits.


Gloat is the practical choice for an agile internal talent marketplace: gig staffing, mentorships, and cross-departmental projects.


Docebo, powered by 365Talents, is the strategic all-in-one engine to detect gaps, deliver learning, manage compliance, and operationalize talent mobility in one ecosystem. It closes the gap between knowing and doing, so your people turn learning into action.


Ready to see the closed loop for yourself?[Take a tour](https://www.docebo.com/take-a-tour/) , or[book a demo](https://www.docebo.com/demo/) . Explore why more than 3,900 companies and 30 million learners worldwide never stop learning with Docebo.


## **FAQs**


### **What are some alternatives to Docebo and Gloat?**


Other names buyers weigh include Degreed, an LXP (learning experience platform); Absorb LMS, a traditional LMS with ecommerce; Cornerstone; and all-in-one HCM suites like Oracle HCM and SAP SuccessFactors. The right alternative depends on whether you prioritize learning, mobility, or core HR.


### **How do Docebo and Gloat support skills-based learning, upskilling, and reskilling initiatives?**


Docebo owns the full loop: it detects skill gaps, delivers targeted training to close them, then tracks and validates the progress. Gloat identifies gaps and can recommend or route learning through a Learning and Reskilling agent, but it relies on a separate LMS or LXP to deliver, track, and validate the upskilling and reskilling itself.


### **How do Docebo and Gloat integrate with existing enterprise systems?**


Both connect to core systems like Workday and SAP SuccessFactors. Docebo adds native connectors for Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom, along with Docebo Connect, using automated recipes without requiring custom code.


### **What role does generative AI play in Docebo compared to Gloat?**


Docebo uses generative AI for content authoring, translation, and assessments, and it curates content from a range of third-party content providers and marketplaces. Gloat focuses its AI on skill parsing and gig matching.


### **How do Docebo and Gloat compare on user experience and mobile app accessibility?**


Docebo offers the Go.Learn mobile app for learning on the go, including offline access. Gloat offers a consumer-grade experience for browsing internal opportunities.


### **Does Gloat offer social learning features, or is that capability unique to Docebo?**


Gloat enables mentorship connections but no formal peer training. Docebo has native social learning built into the platform.
